summary: Chün-fang Yü is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1968–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen, later holding posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001–2018).

Chūta Itō was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Chiba Prefectural Sakura High School, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, First Higher School (~1885–1889), and the University of Tokyo (~1889–1892), where he taught (~1905–1928) before joining Waseda University (~1928–1954).

Clara Sue Kidwell was a scholar in history and archaeology who earned her master's and Ph.D. at the University of Oklahoma (~1963–1970). Her career included positions at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the University of Oklahoma (1995), and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

Clare Carlisle is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002) and held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and King's College London (~2011).

Linguist Claude Hagège studied at institutions including the École Normale Supérieure, École des Langues Orientales, and Paris Descartes University under André Martinet. His career included posts at the CNRS, École Pratique des Hautes Études, University of Poitiers, and Collège de France.

Claude Jacques was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under George Cœdès (~1958–1965). He served as director at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1970–1973) and taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1973–1997).

Claude Lévi-Strauss was an anthropologist and philosopher who studied at the Paris Law Faculty and under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the University of São Paulo, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France (1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at the École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1812–1813) and École polytechnique (~1813–1815), he served in the Sikh Khalsa Army and the Court of Ranjit Singh (~1827–1843).
Claudia Benthien works in linguistics and other fields. She studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~2005).
Claudia Weber is a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and Gregor Ahn.

Claudius Buchanan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge, and served as Vice-Provost at Fort William College starting in 1801.

Claus Oetke was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1968–1983). He taught at Hamburg (~1983–1989) and led the Indology department at the University of Stockholm (1993–2014).

Claus Vogel was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied at the University of Marburg under Dahlmann, Reich, Nobel, Müller, and Rau. He held posts at Marburg, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.

Clyde Kluckhohn was an anthropologist who studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic appointments at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at the CNRS, the University of Lyon, the Sorbonne, and the Institut de civilisation indienne.

Colette Sciberras works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (attested 2002).
Colin Mackenzie studied at Dollar Academy and served as Surveyor-General at the Survey of India (~1815–1821).
Colin Turnbull was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He completed his studies at Westminster School (~1938–1942), Magdalen College (~1942–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).
